headline: Dabur India targets 23% revenue share from its premium product portfolio
hook: Premium tier now generates 20% of sales

modes.bull: Faster growth in high-margin premium products boosts operating margins and earnings quality for Dabur over time.
modes.simple: Dabur is selling more high-end products because they grow much faster than regular items, which can help increase the company's profits.

summary: FMCG major Dabur India is steering its growth strategy toward higher-margin goods as its premium portfolio expands at four times the speed of its core segments. This high-end range currently accounts for 20% of the company's total revenue and is targeted to reach 23%. For Indian retail investors, this shift indicates an aggressive push to protect profit margins against rural demand fluctuations and urban competitive pressures. Higher premium contribution typically enhances operating margins and earnings quality for long-term shareholders.
why_it_matters: Higher-margin product mix could lift Dabur's long-term profitability.
